subject: ACME - Performance SLO/SLA language follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@acme.com>, Acme SRE <sre@acme.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - Performance SLO/SLA follow-up and next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great to sync on your production requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can iterate the SLA language and get this into your procurement queue: 

Recap (from today)
- Latency targets: ACME indicated that P95 generation latency for inference requests should be <=200ms for typical (non-streaming) generation, with P90 considered for some interactive endpoints.
- Streaming: for streaming chat use-cases you emphasized first-byte/first-token time is critical — target is first-byte <=100ms and steady token stream thereafter (you have spikes during long-turn conversations).
- Throughput & concurrency: expected sustained throughput ~1.2M tokens/day with concurrency up to 250 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Measurement: we discussed differences between end-to-end (client -> app -> Redwood -> client) vs server-side (Redwood ingress -> final token emitted). You asked that measurement be representative of your integration (we should define explicit measurement points).

Open items / questions for ACME
1) Confirm whether you want the SLA to reference server-side latency (Redwood edge to token emit) or end-to-end (including your front-end/app). If end-to-end, we'll need to agree on the measurement harness.
2) Confirm the exact percentile(s) you want in the SLA (P90 vs P95 vs both) and the rolling window (30-day typical).
3) Any objections to standard exclusions we typically include (planned maintenance windows, force majeure, customer misconfiguration, network outages outside Redwood control)?
4) Remedies: do you expect service credits for missed SLOs or a different remediation approach? Typical proposal is monthly service credits capped at a percentage of the monthly invoice.

Attachments: redwood_sla_draft_v1.pdf (initial draft), please see inline notes.

Proposed next steps
- Jordan: confirm measurement method (server-side vs end-to-end) and preferred percentiles.
- Acme SRE: share a short synthetic test run (latency logs) if available — helps us align the measurement points.
- Redwood: we'll circulate a tightened SLA draft (call out streaming first-byte semantics) and incorporate legal/ops exclusions.

I'll put together a revised draft and loop David for any legal/ops language. Happy to hop on a quick 30-min follow-up next week if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

--
Attachment: redwood_sla_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 23 KB)

From: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme SRE <sre@acme.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 19:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Performance SLO/SLA language follow-up and next steps

Thanks, Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

Measurement method
- We prefer server-side measurement for the SLA (Redwood ingress -> final token emitted). We'll keep our own end-to-end observability but want the contract to be on what Redwood controls.

Percentiles
- For conversational/chat endpoints we'd like first-byte at P90 <=100ms and P95 <=200ms for the streaming scenario. For non-streaming batch generations we care about P95 <=200ms. If you need a single canonical percentile for the contract, P95 is fine; we'll use P90 internally as an operational target.

Exclusions and remedies
- Exclude planned maintenance and force majeure from measurement. We also ask that customer-side config issues (our proxy misconfig) be excluded where we can demonstrate root cause.
- Remedies: service credits are acceptable. We typically accept monthly credits up to 10% of the monthly invoice for repeated misses, but we'll leave room to negotiate.

Attached a short run of our synthetic test results (attached) — timestamps are client-visible, but note these go through our app layer. Hope this helps you map to the server-side numbers.

We'll review your v2 once it's in — thanks for moving quickly on this.

Jordan Reyes
Senior SRE, Acme Corp
jordan.reyes@acme.com

--
Attachment: acme_latency-test-results.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Performance SLO/SLA language follow-up and next steps

Looping in a couple of legal/ops points we should include in the next draft (low-lift, but important to have explicit language):

1) Measurement window: define P95 as measured over a 30-day rolling window with daily aggregation; specify that transient network failures that are outside Redwood's control are excluded if we can show carrier or client-side fault.
2) Exclusions: planned maintenance (72-hour advance notice window), customer misconfiguration (we require reproducible trace showing config is root cause), DDoS/targeted attacks outside normal threat model.
3) Remedies: propose a standard tiered credit table (example: 99.9% monthly uptime -> 0-1% credits, 99.5-99.9 -> 1-5%, <99.5 -> up to 10%). We should also include a remediation process (root-cause report within 5 business days).
4) Reporting cadence: monthly SLO report delivered via shared Drive link + dashboard access (we can provide a read-only SLO dashboard).

I'll add redline suggestions to the draft (attached) — key is to avoid open-ended monetary liability.

-David
Operations Counsel | Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@acme.com>, Acme SRE <sre@acme.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Performance SLO/SLA language follow-up and next steps

Thanks David & Jordan — incorporated the feedback below and attached a tightened draft (redwood_sla_draft_v2.pdf). Summary of the key changes in v2: 

Measurement definition
- Latency is measured server-side: Redwood ingress timestamp (when request is accepted at the edge) -> timestamp when final token is emitted to the stream/response. For streaming first-byte we measure time-to-first-token; for non-streaming we measure time-to-last-byte.
- Percentiles: P95 is the contract metric; we also include operational P90 targets for streaming first-byte where requested.
- Windowing: P95 computed over a 30-day rolling window with daily aggregation; reporting delivered monthly.

Exclusions
- Planned maintenance (>=72 hours notice), force majeure, customer misconfiguration (requires RFC with traces and reproduction steps), and third-party network outages beyond Redwood control.

Remedies & process
- Tiered service credit table (see section 4 of the draft). Root-cause report within 5 business days for any SLA breach; credits applied to the following invoice. Caps align with David's suggested table.

Streaming specifics
- First-byte SLA: P90 <=100ms, P95 <=200ms for streaming endpoints (as an operational target we can include both; P95 remains the contractual metric). We included an appendix that defines how "first-byte" is measured for WebSocket and SSE flows.

Next steps
- Jordan: confirm you accept server-side measurement and the proposed exclusion list.
- Acme SRE: if you can share a short server-side run (ingress->emit) that maps to your CSV timestamps we can validate the mapping.
- David/Legal: if the redlines look good I'll push v2 to DocuSign for signature and share the Drive link.

Attaching: redwood_sla_draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 28 KB).

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
